q: Vectors can be multiplied in two different ways; the ____ and the vector product.
e: The two products are the scalar product and the vector product. Vectors can be multiplied in two different ways; the scalar product and the vector product.

q: In the scalar product, a ____ can be formed by multiplying two vectors.
e: Dot two vectors and you get a scalar. In the scalar product, a scalar can be formed by multiplying two vectors.

q: The scalar product of vectors A and B is defined as Eq. (2.1), ____.
e: A · B = AB cos θ. That number is the dot product, also called the scalar product. The scalar product of vectors A and B is defined as Eq. (2.1), A · B = AB cos θ.

q: The scalar product is also called the ____.
e: The scalar product is the dot product. Dot product is what this sentence is naming.

q: For example, ____ is the scalar product of force and displacement.
e: Work is the dot product of force and displacement. Work is what this sentence is naming.

q: The scalar product has the ____ property as described by Eq.(2.2) $A \cdot B = B \cdot A$.
e: The dot product commutes: A · B = B · A. The scalar product has the commutative property as described by Eq.(2.2) A · B = B · A. Commutative is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: The vector product of vectors A and B is defined as ____.
e: The vector product is A × B = C, with C = AB sin θ and C perpendicular to the A-B plane. The vector product of vectors A and B is defined as A × B = C.

q: The magnitude of C is $C = AB \sin \theta$ and the direction of C is determined by using the ____.
e: A × B stands perpendicular to the plane of A and B. Parallel would be wrong. The magnitude of C is C = AB sin θ and the direction of C is determined by using the right-hand rule.

q: The direction of C is ____ to the plane that contains A and B.
e: A × B stands perpendicular to the plane of A and B. Parallel would be wrong. The direction of C is perpendicular to the plane that contains A and B.

q: The vector product between two vectors is denoted by a cross (x), hence this product is called the ____.
e: A × B is the cross product, a vector perpendicular to both A and B. The vector product between two vectors is denoted by a cross (x), hence this product is called the cross product. Cross product is what this sentence is naming.

q: The vector product does not obey the ____ property as Eq.(2.4) $A \times B = -(B \times A)$.
e: The cross product anticommutes: A × B = −(B × A). Swap the order and the vector flips. The vector product does not obey the commutative property as Eq.(2.4) A × B = -(B × A).

q: The formulae for the torque and the angular velocity are determined by using the ____.
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. The formulae for the torque and the angular velocity are determined by using the vector product.

q: To use the right-hand rule, first you have to hold up your right hand so that index finger and middle finger are ____ to thumb.
e: Point fingers along A, curl them toward B, and the thumb gives A × B. To use the right-hand rule, first you have to hold up your right hand so that index finger and middle finger are perpendicular to thumb. Perpendicular is what this sentence is naming.

q: Now rotate your hand such that your index finger points in the direction of A and your ____ points in the direction of B.
e: Right-hand rule: index along A, middle finger along B, thumb along A × B. Now rotate your hand such that your index finger points in the direction of A and your middle finger points in the direction of B. Middle finger is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: Your ____ will point in the direction of the cross product $A \times B$.
e: A × B is the cross product, a vector perpendicular to both A and B. Your thumb will point in the direction of the cross product A × B. Thumb is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: Torque is a vector quantity and its vector form can be expressed as ____.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. Torque is a vector quantity and its vector form can be expressed as tau = r × F.

q: The magnitude of the moment of force (or) torque is defined as the product of force and the ____ from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. The magnitude of the moment of force (or) torque is defined as the product of force and the perpendicular distance from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum.

q: The moment of inertia of an object is defined as the sum of the products obtained by multiplying the ____ in a given object and the square of its distance from the axis.
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. The moment of inertia of an object is defined as the sum of the products obtained by multiplying the mass of each particle in a given object and the square of its distance from the axis. Mass of each particle is the term used with moment inertia object defined as sum.

q: The angular momentum L of an object is defined as the product of its moment of inertia I and ____.
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. The angular momentum L of an object is defined as the product of its moment of inertia I and angular velocity ω.

q: When a force is applied to an object, it can turn the object about a certain point known as the pivot(or) the ____.
e: When a force is applied to an object, it can turn the object about a certain point known as the pivot(or) the fulcrum. The name used here is fulcrum.

q: The turning effect of a force about a particular fulcrum is measured by the ____ of that force (or) torque.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. The turning effect of a force about a particular fulcrum is measured by the moment of that force (or) torque.

q: Torque is a ____ quantity and its vector form can be expressed as the Eq.(2.5), $\tau = r \times F$.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. Torque is a vector quantity and its vector form can be expressed as the Eq.(2.5), tau = r × F.

q: The magnitude of the moment of force (or) torque $\tau$ is defined as the product of the force F and the ____ from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. The magnitude of the moment of force (or) torque tau is defined as the product of the force F and the perpendicular distance from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum.

q: The equation for the magnitude of torque can be written as $\tau = Fr \sin \theta =$ ____.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. The equation for the magnitude of torque can be written as tau = Fr sin θ = Fd.

q: The perpendicular distance from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum ($d = r \sin \theta$) is also called the ____ of a force.
e: The perpendicular distance from the line of action of the force to the fulcrum (d = r sin θ) is also called the moment arm of a force. The name used here is moment arm.

q: The ____ of a force is a line along which a force is considered to act.
e: The line of action of a force is a line along which a force is considered to act. Line of action is what this statement is using.

q: In SI units, the moment of force (or) torque is measured in newton metre (N m), which is never written as ____.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. In SI units, the moment of force (or) torque is measured in newton metre (N m), which is never written as joule.

q: According to ____, $F = ma = mr\alpha$.
e: According to Newton's second law, F = ma = mrα. Newton's second law is what this statement is using.

q: Torque due to tangential force; $\tau = Fr = (mr\alpha)r$.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. Torque due to tangential force; tau = Fr = (mrα)r.

q: The torque equation simplifies to $\tau =$ ____.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. The torque equation simplifies to tau = mr²α.

q: In Eq.(2.7) the terms $mr^2$ is the ____ of that particle about the axis (I).
e: In Eq.(2.7) the terms mr² is the moment of inertia of that particle about the axis (I). Moment of inertia is what this statement is using.

q: The rotational equivalent of Newton's second law is written as ____.
e: The rotational equivalent of Newton's second law is written as tau = Iα. Leave the relation as tau = Iα.

q: The moment of inertia of an object composed of multiple particles is $I = $ ____.
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. The moment of inertia of an object composed of multiple particles is I = m_1r_1² + m_2r_2² + m_3r_3² +. + m_nr_n².

q: The moment of inertia I can be written in summation notation as ____.
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. The moment of inertia I can be written in summation notation as I = Sigma mr².

q: The moment of inertia of an object is defined as the sum of the products obtained by multiplying the mass of each particle in a given object and the ____ from the axis.
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. The moment of inertia of an object is defined as the sum of the products obtained by multiplying the mass of each particle in a given object and the square of its distance from the axis. Square of its distance is the term used with moment inertia object defined as sum.

q: The moment of inertia is a ____ and the SI unit is $kg \cdot m^2$.
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. The moment of inertia is a scalar and the SI unit is kg · m².

q: The moment of inertia must be specified with respect to a chosen ____.
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. The moment of inertia must be specified with respect to a chosen axis of rotation.

q: The ____ of a particular object is a point at which all its weight may be considered to act.
e: The centre of gravity of a particular object is a point at which all its weight may be considered to act. Centre of gravity is what this statement is using.

q: For an object of regular shape and ____, the centre of gravity is at its geometrical center.
e: For an object of regular shape and uniform density, the centre of gravity is at its geometrical center. Uniform density is what this statement is using.

q: For example, the weight of a metre stick of uniform density is considered to be acting at the ____ (its mid-point).
e: Density is mass per unit volume, ρ = m/V. For example, the weight of a metre stick of uniform density is considered to be acting at the 50 cm mark (its mid-point). 50 cm mark is what this sentence is naming.

q: The moment of inertia of a solid sphere about its axis of rotation is ____.
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. The moment of inertia of a solid sphere about its axis of rotation is I = (2)/(5)MR².

q: When the system is in ____, there is no linear motion and no rotational motion.
e: When the system is in static equilibrium, there is no linear motion and no rotational motion. Static equilibrium is what this statement is using.

q: Under this condition, the forces on it must be balanced and the ____ on it must also be balanced.
e: Under this condition, the forces on it must be balanced and the moment of the forces on it must also be balanced. Moment of the forces is what this statement is using.

q: The conditions of static equilibrium are (1) the ____ on the system is zero, $\Sigma F = 0$, and (2) the resultant torque on the system is zero, $\Sigma \tau = 0$.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. The conditions of static equilibrium are (1) the resultant force on the system is zero, Sigma F = 0, and (2) the resultant torque on the system is zero, Sigma tau = 0.

q: The conditions of static equilibrium are (1) the resultant force on the system is zero, $\Sigma F = 0$, and (2) the ____ on the system is zero, $\Sigma \tau = 0$.
e: The conditions of static equilibrium are (1) the resultant force on the system is zero, Sigma F = 0, and (2) the resultant torque on the system is zero, Sigma tau = 0. Resultant torque is what this statement is using.

q: The condition necessary for a pivoted object to be in balance is given by the ____.
e: The condition necessary for a pivoted object to be in balance is given by the principle of moments. Principle of moments is what this statement is using.

q: This principle states that if an object such as a bar (or) a plank is to be in balance, the total ____ about the fulcrum must equal the total anticlockwise moment.
e: This principle states that if an object such as a bar (or) a plank is to be in balance, the total clockwise moment about the fulcrum must equal the total anticlockwise moment. Clockwise moment is what this statement is using.

q: The examples of the application of this principle are building site crane, ____ etc.
e: The examples of the application of this principle are building site crane, beam balance etc. Beam balance is what this statement is using.

q: In rotational motion, the angular momentum of an object is defined as the product of its ____ and the angular velocity.
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. In rotational motion, the angular momentum of an object is defined as the product of its moment of inertia and the angular velocity.

q: For linear motion, the momentum is equal to the product of the ____ and the velocity.
e: For linear motion, the momentum is equal to the product of the mass and the velocity. Mass is what this statement is using.

q: The moment of inertia is analogous to mass and the angular velocity is analogous to the ____.
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. The moment of inertia is analogous to mass and the angular velocity is analogous to the linear velocity.

q: The formula for angular momentum is ____.
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. The formula for angular momentum is L = Iω.

q: In SI units, since the unit of moment of inertia is $kg \cdot m^2$ and that of angular velocity is $rad \cdot s^{-1}$, the unit of angular momentum is ____.
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. In SI units, since the unit of moment of inertia is kg · m² and that of angular velocity is rad · s^-1, the unit of angular momentum is kg · m² · s^-1.

q: Angular momentum is a ____ quantity.
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. Angular momentum is a vector quantity.

q: The law of ____ is also one fundamental law of physics.
e: The fundamental is the lowest standing-wave frequency. Higher ones are harmonics or overtones. The law of conservation of angular momentum is also one fundamental law of physics.

q: This law states that: If there is no ____ acting on an isolated system, the total angular momentum of the system is constant.
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. This law states that: If there is no net external torque acting on an isolated system, the total angular momentum of the system is constant.

q: In symbols, if $\Sigma \tau = 0$, then ____.
e: In symbols, if Sigma tau = 0, then L = constant. Leave the relation as L = constant.

q: Her rate of spin (angular speed) increases greatly as her ____ decreases by pulling in her arms inwards.
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. Her rate of spin (angular speed) increases greatly as her moment of inertia decreases by pulling in her arms inwards.

q: If she wants to slow down her rotation, she will stretch her arms ____.
e: If she wants to slow down her rotation, she will stretch her arms outwards. Outwards is what this statement is using.

q: When her moment of inertia increases, the rotational angular speed will ____.
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. When her moment of inertia increases, the rotational angular speed will decrease.

q: An example of conservation of angular momentum is seen in an ____ performing a spin.
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. An example of conservation of angular momentum is seen in an ice skater performing a spin.

q: A ____ who is rotating when jumping off the board does not need to make any physical effort to continue rotating.
e: A springboard diver who is rotating when jumping off the board does not need to make any physical effort to continue rotating. Springboard diver is what this statement is using.

q: The moment of inertia of a disc is given by the formula ____.
e: Moment of inertia is Σ m r². It says how the mass is spread about the axis. The moment of inertia of a disc is given by the formula (1)/(2)MR².
